name_note: The GTDB species holds genomes named Corynebacterium lehmanniae, Corynebacterium haemomassiliense and Corynebacterium faecium in NCBI, so it is broader than the published species Corynebacterium lehmanniae.

sentences.text: Corynebacterium lehmanniae was proposed as a new species among eight Corynebacterium strains isolated from urine samples of healthy women or women diagnosed with overactive bladder.
The strains characterised in that work were Gram stain positive, rod to coccoid shaped, nonmotile, catalase positive and oxidase negative.

The genus Corynebacterium is reported to be frequently found in the female urinary microbiome, and commonly used methods there had limited resolution for discriminating Corynebacterium at species level.
Corynebacterium haemomassiliense was described from a blood specimen obtained from a 59-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms.

Two cases of human infection caused by Corynebacterium haemomassiliense-like organisms have been reported, with both strains multidrug-resistant but susceptible to vancomycin, meropenem and linezolid.
